items.setupText: Choose the version suited to a formal report that keeps 'to' immediately before the relative pronoun.

items.setupText: Choose the relative phrase that preserves the plan as the subject of negotiations, not as a method or source of opposition.

items.setupText: Choose the wording that clearly identifies the reason for the rejection.
items.taskText: The application was rejected because it arrived late. The decision letter did not explain that reason.

The reason why the letter arrived late was the application's rejection.
The reason for which the application was rejected was not explained in the letter.
items.answer: The reason for which the application was rejected was not explained in the letter.
items.explanation: For which links the reason to the rejection; the main clause preserves its absence from the letter.

items.setupText: Choose the sentence that presents the clinic's free service as extra information about the already identified clinic.

The clinic will offer free check-ups when it moves in June.
The clinic, which offers free check-ups, will move in June.
items.answer: The clinic, which offers free check-ups, will move in June.
items.explanation: The comma-separated 'which' clause adds information about the already identified clinic; the move remains the main statement.

items.setupText: Choose the interpretation supported by the sentence.

items.setupText: Choose the version that keeps both the owner and the place of storage unchanged.

audit.pedagogicalValue: Links a location to its owner within a longer relative phrase.
audit.levelReason: B2 tracks possession, storage, and a loan across a fronted prepositional relative.

items.setupText: Choose the sentence that preserves the two separate descriptions of the software.

rationales.As additional information about the revi: Commas make the concern supplementary information about the identified reviewers rather than a restriction selecting some of them.

items.setupText: Choose the interpretation that keeps the source of the judgment clear.

The lawyer doubted the witness, despite the detail of the account.
The lawyer accepted the witness's account because it was detailed.

rationales.The lawyer accepted the witness's accoun: Nevertheless contrasts the negative assessment with the detailed account; it does not report acceptance.
rationales.The lawyer doubted the witness, despite: 'Whom' is the person assessed by the lawyer; 'nevertheless' contrasts that assessment with the detailed testimony.

audit.microSkill: Attributed evaluation in an object relative
audit.pedagogicalValue: Separates a participant's judgment from the narrator's assertion.

items.setupText: Choose the paraphrase that expresses a mechanism rather than a setting.

The procedure provided a means for tenants to challenge disputed charges.
items.answer: The procedure provided a means for tenants to challenge disputed charges.

rationales.The procedure provided a means for tenan: 'Whereby' means 'by which' here: the procedure is the means enabling tenants to challenge charges.
rationales.The procedure recorded the occasions on: Could presents an available mechanism, not a record of previous challenges.
rationales.The procedure identified the location wh: A physical location for receiving charges is different from a process for contesting them.

findings: The appeals-review whereby gap could wrongly reject abstract where and repeated after in its tail.
audit.microSkill: Whereby expresses an enabling means
audit.pedagogicalValue: Distinguishes mechanism from setting without declaring abstract where ungrammatical.

items.setupText: Choose the edit that explicitly makes the delay, rather than the permit, the cause of increased costs.

rationales.The contractor received the permit late,: A delay provides an explicit antecedent for which and assigns the cost increase to late receipt.
rationales.The contractor received the permit for t: This attaches the relative to work and does not isolate the delay as the cause.

audit.levelReason: C1 edits causal reference where a bare which could be read too broadly.
audit.similarityNote: Unlike the B2 decision example, the learner must repair an underspecified antecedent.

items.setupText: Choose the conclusion that follows without adding an unstated claim.
items.taskText: The delegates, three of whose proposals were adopted, asked for feedback on the remaining proposals.

audit.pedagogicalValue: Distinguishes counting possessions from counting their owners or distributing counts per owner.

items.setupText: Choose the sentence that preserves the difference between method and result.
items.taskText: The audit examined the way in which complaints were handled, not whether complainants were satisfied.

The audit established why complainants accepted the decisions.

The audit investigated the process used to deal with complaints.
items.answer: The audit investigated the process used to deal with complaints.

rationales.The audit established why complainants a: Reasons for accepting decisions concern reactions, not the handling method identified by the way in which.
rationales.The audit checked whether complaints had: Whether decisions were favourable evaluates outcomes rather than how complaints were processed.
rationales.The audit investigated the process used: 'The way in which' introduces manner or method; it identifies the handling process as the object of examination.

audit.microSkill: The way in which identifies a method
audit.pedagogicalValue: Separates procedural examination from evaluation of outcomes or recipients' reactions.
audit.levelReason: C1 reads an abstract manner relative against neighbouring evaluative alternatives.

items.setupText: Choose the interpretation that correctly identifies who was interviewed.

rationales.The supervisor was interviewed; the anal: The committee interviewed the analyst's supervisor inside the relative clause; the main-clause invitation went to the analyst.
rationales.The committee interviewed the analyst an: This swaps the interviewee and the recipient of the invitation.
rationales.The supervisor interviewed the committee: The committee is the interviewer, not the group interviewed by the supervisor.

findings: The original grant-recipient sentence repeated a formal whom gap.
An initial embedded-belief replacement overlapped with B2's reported repairer, so the recheck substituted a possessive object-relative problem.

audit.pedagogicalValue: Keeps a head noun distinct from its associated person when different actions apply to them.
audit.levelReason: C1 tracks the committee, supervisor, and analyst through an object relative and passive main clause.
audit.similarityNote: The relative's possessed noun is its object, unlike whose roof or whose methods subjects.

items.setupText: Choose the interpretation of 'setting where' in context.

items.answer: The training provided circumstances favourable to open questioning.
items.explanation: 'Where' introduces an abstract setting: circumstances in which staff felt able to question practice.

rationales.The training designated a room in which: 'Setting' can describe circumstances rather than a physical room, and privacy is not the same as freedom from embarrassment.
rationales.The training provided circumstances favo: 'Where' introduces an abstract setting: circumstances in which staff felt able to question practice.
rationales.The training introduced a requirement to: 'Could question' creates an opportunity, not a requirement that each questioned practice be revised.

findings: The second appeals-review whereby item could penalize a legitimate abstract where reading and repeated the same process frame.
audit.microSkill: Abstract where expresses enabling circumstances
audit.pedagogicalValue: Distinguishes a supportive setting from prescribed method or guaranteed outcome.
audit.levelReason: C1 interprets an abstract locative relative and the limited force of could.
audit.similarityNote: Provides a valid abstract where use, complementing rather than competing unfairly with whereby.

items.setupText: Choose the reading that preserves the scope of 'none'.

items.answer: The four interviewees lacked merger-management experience.

rationales.The interview panel lacked merger-manage: 'Whom' refers to the candidates, not the panel members assessing them.
rationales.The panel selected someone outside the f: The relative describes the interviewees' experience; it does not show that the eventual selection came from elsewhere.
rationales.The four candidates had managed mergers: 'None had managed a merger' denies that experience; it does not restrict the denial to experience as a director.
rationales.The four interviewees lacked merger-mana: 'None of whom' applies the lack of merger-management experience to the four interviewees, without extending it to the panel or other candidates.

findings: The twice-revised lesson plan repeated a comma-relative form choice and an arbitrary academic tail.
audit.microSkill: Domain of a negative partitive relative
audit.pedagogicalValue: Limits a negative generalization to the explicitly named set.
audit.levelReason: C1 distinguishes set-level information from unsupported claims about selection or wider populations.

findings: The repeated experienced-applicant whose item did not test the status of information in a relative clause.

rationales.The backup system prevented the power fa: 'Without which' refers to the backup system and frames destruction as what would have happened in its absence.

findings: The third appeals-review whereby gap repeated an abstract process and potentially valid where distractor.

items.setupText: Choose the sentence that unambiguously refers to the organization's recommendations, not its members' personal recommendations.

rationales.Any applicant who was shortlisted had th: The negative statement rules out a shortlisted applicant lacking certification, so shortlisted applicants had it.
rationales.The panel shortlisted applicants accordi: The relative distinguishes possession from absence of certification, not recency.

findings: The fourth tribunal-whose-jurisdiction item repeated possession without examining restrictive scope under a quantifier.
audit.microSkill: Negative quantified head restricted by a relative
audit.pedagogicalValue: Derives a necessary property of selected people without assuming its sufficiency or their existence.
audit.levelReason: C2 interprets the logical effect of a defining relative under no and avoids a reversed implication.
audit.similarityNote: The negative quantifier precedes a restrictive relative, unlike supplementary information outside negation.

items.setupText: Choose the rewrite that explicitly means a different physical copy with matching terms, not the very document signed earlier.
items.taskText: The witness was shown the same contract as the director had signed.
options: The witness was shown the contract that bore the director's original signature.
The witness was shown the signed contract, which the director had kept in the file.
The witness was shown the very contract that the director had signed.
The witness was shown a separate copy whose terms matched those of the signed contract.
items.answer: The witness was shown a separate copy whose terms matched those of the signed contract.
items.explanation: Separate copy fixes physical non-identity, while whose terms matched preserves equivalence of contractual content.

rationales.The witness was shown the contract that: The original signature identifies the signed document, not explicitly a separate matching copy.
rationales.The witness was shown a separate copy wh: Separate copy fixes physical non-identity, while whose terms matched preserves equivalence of contractual content.
rationales.The witness was shown the signed contrac: This again identifies the shown document as the signed contract rather than clarifying a different copy.
rationales.The witness was shown the very contract: The very contract emphasizes identity of the physical document, contrary to the editing goal.

findings: The fourth witness-partitive gap repeated several of whom without an advanced reference distinction.
audit.microSkill: Disambiguating identity versus equivalence around the same ... as
audit.pedagogicalValue: Avoids assuming that the same fixes whether an object or merely its content is identical.
audit.levelReason: C2 resolves a subtle identity ambiguity by choosing an explicit possessive relative and head noun.
audit.similarityNote: The ambiguity concerns type versus physical token, not attachment to a neighbouring noun.

items.setupText: Choose the reading of 'such information as' in context.
items.taskText: The reviewer assessed the project using such information as the organizers were willing to release.
options: The reviewer worked within the information the organizers were prepared to make available.
The reviewer chose information similar to material the organizers had withheld.
The organizers released the information that the reviewer had already assessed.
The reviewer assessed examples of information rather than the project itself.
items.answer: The reviewer worked within the information the organizers were prepared to make available.
items.explanation: The 'as' clause restricts the available information to what the organizers were willing to release; it need not mean a complete record.

rationales.The reviewer chose information similar t: 'Such...as' identifies the available information here; it does not describe similarity to withheld material.
rationales.The organizers released the information: The relative limits the information by willingness to release it, not by an earlier review of that information.
rationales.The reviewer assessed examples of inform: 'Such information as' is not an examples list here, and 'project' remains the object of 'assessed'.
rationales.The reviewer worked within the informati: The 'as' clause restricts the available information to what the organizers were willing to release; it need not mean a complete record.

findings: The fourth statute-genitive relative recycled meaning of which with generic rejection messages.
audit.microSkill: Such ... as limits an available informational domain
audit.pedagogicalValue: Recognizes a restrictive as construction instead of reading such as as an example marker or similarity comparison.
audit.levelReason: C2 interprets a formal availability-limiting construction and avoids assuming full disclosure.
audit.similarityNote: Restrictive such...as differs from the parenthetical evaluative such as they were at C1.

items.setupText: Choose the wording that makes the limit apply to which proposal was rejected, not to who rejected it.
items.taskText: Of several proposals, the board rejected only the proposal requiring an outside audit.
options: The proposal that required an outside audit was rejected only by the board.
Only the board rejected the proposal that required an outside audit.
The only proposal that the board rejected was the one requiring an outside audit.
The proposal that only the board rejected required an outside audit.
items.answer: The only proposal that the board rejected was the one requiring an outside audit.
items.explanation: The only proposal places exclusivity on the head restricted by that the board rejected, singling out one rejected proposal.

rationales.The proposal that required an outside au: Only by the board limits the rejecting agent, not the set of rejected proposals.
rationales.Only the board rejected the proposal tha: Only the board again focuses on the agent and leaves open what else it rejected.
rationales.The only proposal that the board rejecte: The only proposal places exclusivity on the head restricted by that the board rejected, singling out one rejected proposal.
rationales.The proposal that only the board rejecte: Only inside the relative attaches to the board as agent rather than limiting how many proposals it rejected.

findings: The final mechanism-whereby item repeated the same advanced-looking but elementary form choice.
audit.microSkill: Focus scope around an object relative and its head
audit.pedagogicalValue: Positions only so that it restricts the intended set rather than the agent inside the relative.
audit.levelReason: C2 edits closely related grammatical sentences whose focus placement changes the asserted exclusivity.
audit.similarityNote: The distinction is focus scope across a relative boundary, not relative pronoun form or attachment.
